blocks.heading: Stakeholder objectives
blocks.text: An objective is a result a person or group wants to achieve. Consumers may seek value and dependable quality; workers may seek pay, safety and security; managers may seek effective performance and career progress. Owners may seek profit and long-term survival. Finance providers may seek repayment or a return consistent with risk. The community may seek jobs and useful services without excessive disturbance. These objectives can overlap but do not necessarily have equal priority.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: The owners of Omuti Foods are considering a later opening time, higher wages and a price increase. Higher pay may support workers but increase costs. A higher price could help cover those costs, yet reduce value for some customers and weaken demand. The lender is interested in whether the bakery can continue meeting repayments. Residents may care about delivery noise as well as employment. A decision should identify who gains or loses, rather than assume the owners’ objective represents every stakeholder.

blocks.heading: Consumer objectives
blocks.text: Consumers may seek value for money and reliable product quality. Convenient access and a safe, dependable product can also matter.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented household buys bread before school. A low price has limited value to that household if the shop is closed when bread is needed.

blocks.heading: Worker objectives
blocks.text: Workers may seek fair pay and safe working conditions. Security, development and satisfaction can also influence their priorities.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented bakery worker is learning to operate new equipment. Training and a safe procedure can matter alongside the wage because the worker needs to perform the task confidently.

blocks.heading: Manager objectives
blocks.text: Managers may seek to achieve business targets and use resources effectively. They may also value recognition, responsibility and career development.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented manager is responsible for a Friday delivery. The manager needs enough resources and cooperation to meet that target, rather than merely being given a title.

blocks.heading: Owner objectives
blocks.text: Owners may seek a return on their investment and the continued survival of the enterprise. Some also prioritise growth, independence or a social purpose.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented bakery owner chooses between withdrawing cash and replacing an unreliable oven. Taking more cash now may conflict with maintaining the equipment needed for future sales.

blocks.heading: Finance-provider objectives
blocks.text: A lender may seek repayment and interest consistent with the risk. An investor may seek returns and information about how the business performs.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented lender considers financing a bakery oven. The lender’s interest is not the same as a customer’s: expected repayment and risk matter, and approval is not guaranteed.

blocks.heading: Community objectives
blocks.text: The wider community may seek employment and useful local services. It may also want less pollution, congestion and disturbance.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: An invented bakery creates local jobs but receives noisy deliveries early in the morning. Residents can welcome employment while asking for a less disruptive delivery arrangement.
